parts.note: read as the head of the word 'dunder', its first letter D
left over means remaining, so over can stand for left

explanation.surface: A fool has sailed out of the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool, but it is read literally as the head of 'dunder'. DOVER is the English Channel port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the best-known English ferry harbour, on the Kent coast facing France.

indicators.note: one piece holding another inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: an ace is the card worth one
pie is a dish of food

explanation.surface: Every person is laden with something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the single-spot playing card here, and 'carries' signals that the second piece is held inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning for every one, as in 'a pound apiece'.

clue.text: Footballer behaving in a childish way?

definitions.text: Footballer behaving in a childish way?

parts.words: Footballer behaving in a childish way?
parts.note: a footballer who runs the ball forward with short kicks, punning on the slobbering of a baby

explanation.surface: A football player acting like an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who runs with the ball at his feet is said to dribble, as babies do with saliva.

indicators.note: reorganising rearranges the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper plans to overhaul the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accounts' suggests bookkeeping in a shop, but it means tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts here are narrated tales, as in an account of events.

parts.note: to be after something is to want it
the lot means everything, all

explanation.surface: Greedy for everything, come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in spite of what has been said or happened, nonetheless.

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece written on another comes below it, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: to check is to hold back or deter
a gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man inspects another bloke who does the cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means one piece is placed after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a washing agent, a substance used for cleansing.

parts.note: a cooper makes casks and barrels
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A cask-maker mocks a suggestion of teamwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' suggests mockery, but it is the past of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to work together, combining efforts with others.

clue.text: Present that's just not on with royalty

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A gift considered unacceptable when given to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a common crossword stand-in for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out for acceptance, a synonym of proffer.

clue.text: Elegant Greek character-and cold with it

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A stylish Greek person who is rather chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable.

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army soldiers
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Think back to the troops and the weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' suggests a weapon but is a limb. RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is to bring back to mind.

clue.text: A man two top journalists paid attention to

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: two asks for the piece to be written twice

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, the top journalist

explanation.surface: A man listened to a pair of senior newspaper staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Heeded means took notice of, listened to.

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin with its hair

explanation.definitionFit: A fell is an old word for animal pelt, and fell is also the past of falling down.

clue.text: Out of petty cash to obtain switch

parts.note: ex means out of or from
change is loose coins, petty cash

explanation.surface: Taking money from the office float to swap it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange is to swap or trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Guides cried about some rocky heights

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of cried are turned around into a new order

parts.note: tors are rocky hilltops, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Mountain leaders shouted on some craggy peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes DIREC from CRIED. A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors are people who guide or steer an enterprise.

clue.text: See how cinders may be utilised

indicators.note: using the letters of cinders as raw material to make a new word

explanation.surface: Observe how cinders might be put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or make out.

clue.text: Urban centre offering extended charging facilities

parts.note: credit is the facility to charge goods to an account
on means continued, carried forward, as in 'and so on'

explanation.surface: A town providing extra time to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: CREDITON is a small market town in Devon, England. The surface suggests generous terms for paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Crediton is a Devon market town, so a place where people live and trade.

parts.note: a death, or else the huge profit a lucky speculator is said to make

explanation.surface: A deadly outcome of gambling on the markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a big profit is idiomatically making a killing, which is also a slaying.

parts.note: late can mean former, as in 'the late chairman'

explanation.surface: Creep inside after the agreed time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sneak' looks like a verb but is a noun, a telltale.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a telltale who passes on secrets, a grass.

clue.text: Train maybe after church, being reliable

indicators.note: after puts the train piece behind the church piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: maybe shows the letters of train are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A rail service following the church, being dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the vehicle's letters, and 'after' puts them behind the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain means sure, dependable.

clue.text: Combine making charge about trade collapse

indicators.note: the fee goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: collapse breaks up the letters of trade into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Imposing a levy concerning the failure of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' rearranges the letters of 'trade', and 'about' wraps the charge around that new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to unite into a league or alliance.

clue.text: A place to grow flowers when retired

parts.note: a flower bed is a plot for growing plants

explanation.surface: A garden plot ready for when one stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests stopping work, but it means having gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means in bed, as one is after retiring for the night.

definitions.meaning: a dope is a stupid person
a pudding of crushed fruit and cream, as in gooseberry

explanation.definitionFit: A fool is both an idiot and a creamy dessert of stewed fruit.

indicators.note: a new design rearranges the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A monarch's gown is not newly styled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innovative design' rearranges ROBE and NO. Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the fairy king in Shakespeare's comedy.

definitions.meaning: a report is a noise, as of a gun

explanation.definitionFit: Sound means valid of an argument, and is also a noise, as a gun's report is.

parts.note: S is south, one quarter of the compass

indicators.note: changing alters the order of the letters of tried

explanation.surface: Someone attempting a new walking pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' turns TRIED into TRIDE. South is one of the compass's four quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long pace or step.

definitions.meaning: of a machine, switched into action

explanation.definitionFit: A switched-on device has been activated, and someone excited is aroused in the same idiom.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain chart hits cause upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'give offence' as the definition, but the answer is a noun; 'offence' alone is the definition and 'give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Stiff, as any bird-watcher might well be

definitions.text: as any bird-watcher might well be
definitions.meaning: heading for, or confined in, a shelter used to watch birds

explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound means narrow-minded and rigid, and literally means bound for a birdwatcher's shelter.
